source_observations.finding: Statement/v1 binds an attestation to one or more immutable subjects identified by digest and separately identifies predicateType; subject matching is digest-based rather than inferred from names or content semantics.
The Link predicate models one executed step with subject as products/outputs and materials as input ResourceDescriptors, while name/command/byproducts/environment describe the step context.

The Runtime Trace predicate identifies the monitor instance/configuration and monitored process separately from the trace log; it is monitor-technology agnostic and explicitly warns that asynchronous eBPF file-access observation provides weaker digest guarantees than synchronous tracing.
The Envelope layer recommends authenticated payload plus payloadType via DSSE-like envelopes; consumers must verify the payload/signature rather than trusting media type metadata.

An attestation Bundle is not authenticated as a whole; the specification explicitly calls out deletion, replay of obsolete attestations and injection of invalid/irrelevant attestations as threats. Bundle order must not carry semantics.

counterhypotheses.statement: Existing F2 receipts already bind inputs, outputs, provenance and generations sufficiently; an in-toto-inspired layer would add schema complexity without detecting new failures.
counterhypotheses.next_falsifier: At E2, map current high-value WP507/WP105 receipts field-by-field and test whether an in-toto-style subject/material/predicate envelope catches any replay, wrong-input, wrong-output or observer-strength ambiguity not already rejected.

counterhypotheses.statement: Cryptographic envelope signing is unnecessary inside the current single-authority repository evidence path and would add cost without increasing useful assurance.
counterhypotheses.next_falsifier: Identify a concrete threat or cross-boundary handoff where source/hash binding alone cannot distinguish tampering or provenance substitution; otherwise keep signing out of the immediate F2 path.
